name: zettau
label: zeta Tau (B2 IIIpe shell star, SB 133 d)
sources: Wikipedia infobox (read 2026-10-08) and the papers it cites: V 3.01, B2 IIIpe Be/shell star, SB 133 d, T_eff 15500 K, R 5.5 Rsun, M 11.2 Msun, d 140 pc
notes: No interferometric diameter exists: theta_LD = 2R/d = 0.365 mas from the quoted radius and distance; the Pathfinder would be its first measurement.
Claret & Bloemen 2011 linear law of Spica (hot B star) as the limb-darkening fallback; NewEra does not cover T_eff > 12 000 K.
T_eff 15 500 K as quoted (low for B2 III; the disk veils the photosphere).

line_disk: the H-alpha decretion disk (several mas), seen only by channels on the line (runner g2, array mode); resolved out at 300-530 m, where an H-alpha filter measures the photospheric fraction of the H-alpha light.

summary.components: B2 IIIpe Be/shell star, SB 133 d

sources: Tycner et al. 2004, AJ 127, 1194 (NPOI, narrow-band H-alpha): elliptical Gaussian major axis 3.14 +/- 0.21 mas, minor/major 0.310 +/- 0.072, PA -62.3 +/- 4.4 deg
Naze et al. 2024, arXiv:2406.15161 (BeSS spectra, 2022-2024): EW(H-alpha) between -9 and -16 A, a shell profile with a variable central absorption
notes: axis_ratio 3.226 = 1 / 0.310; pa_deg 117.7 = -62.3 + 180. Quirrenbach et al. 1994 (Mk III): 3.55 mas, 0.30, PA -59.
ew_nm 1.3 is the middle of the 2022-2024 range; line_fwhm_kms 400 is a guess for the double-peaked shell profile, modelled as one Gaussian. A spectrum taken with the observations must replace both.
